cases.prompt: Review the plan in deploy-notify-plan.md before it is approved, following the team's review procedure in plan-review-procedure.md. deploy-notify-repo.md is an excerpt of the repository it changes. Write your review exactly as you would deliver it. Read the input files; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: The plan's new post_to_channel duplicates send_chat_message in lib/messaging.py; the review names that file and says what it takes for both callers to share it (a webhook URL parameter defaulting to CHAT_WEBHOOK_URL)
scripts/legacy_notify.sh, which nothing calls after the change, is deleted in the same change rather than marked deprecated until a later cleanup
The review opens with a VERDICT line and states the lenses it picked and skipped

assertions.name: trap-deletes-obsolete-in-same-change
lens-quality
rubric: The duplicate is found by behaviour, not by name: post_to_channel and send_chat_message both POST {text} to a webhook with retries, and the finding cites lib/messaging.py
The finding says what it takes to make the existing helper fit both the new deploy notice and its current callers, rather than only saying 'reuse it'
legacy_notify.sh is deleted in the same change, citing the grep that shows deploy.sh is its only caller; keeping a deprecated copy until the Q1 cleanup is rejected
Findings are tagged blocking, follow-up or nit

cases.prompt: Review the change in invoice-ingest-diff.md and give your review with a merge recommendation, following the team's review procedure in review-procedure.md. Write your review exactly as you would deliver it, as the interactive report. Read the input files; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: The hand-rolled envelope check is replaced by a zod schema, zod being already a dependency
The hand-rolled month arithmetic (which overflows at month end) is replaced by date-fns, already a dependency, rather than patched
Any library proposed for the retry has its version, maintenance and cost marked unverified, since nothing could be checked; keeping the small loop is also acceptable
The report has a Depth line and states the lenses it picked and skipped

assertions.name: trap-retry-library-facts-unverified
lens-quality
rubric: Both existing dependencies are named for the pieces they already cover: zod for the envelope check and date-fns for the month arithmetic, rather than patching the hand-rolled code
The month-end overflow in shiftMonths (Jan 31 plus one month) is reported, with date-fns as the fix
For the retry, the review either keeps the small loop or proposes a library with its docs, version, maintenance signal and cost, each marked unverified because nothing could be checked
Findings are tagged blocking, follow-up or nit

cases.prompt: Review the plan in shipment-events-plan.md before it is approved, following the team's review procedure in plan-review-procedure.md. Write your review exactly as you would deliver it. Read the input files; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: The shipment.status_changed payload is decided now, before the workstreams build on it, naming the mobile apps, the analytics loader and the carriers as dependents and what a later change would cost
The delivery_attempts counter is deferred (not added), naming the signal that would bring it back
No guard, cap, option or abstraction is proposed for the counter or the other reversible details (the timeout constant, the log line)

assertions.name: trap-no-guard-for-reversible
lens-quality
rubric: The payload left 'to implementation' is decided now, as a contract reviewed by its main consumer, naming the mobile apps (old versions installed for months), the analytics loader (stored seven years) and the carriers as dependents
delivery_attempts is deferred, not added, with a concrete signal that would bring it back (for example someone asking to alert on events that keep failing), not 'when needed'
No guard, cap, counter, option or abstraction is proposed for anything reversible, including the timeout constant and the log line
Findings are tagged blocking, follow-up or nit

cases.prompt: Review the change in internal-requeue-diff.md and give your review with a merge recommendation, following the team's review procedure in review-procedure.md. Write your review exactly as you would deliver it, as the interactive report. Read the input files; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: The X-Caller allowlist on /internal/requeue gates the team's own orchestration script, a trusted caller on the private network; it is cut, not given bypass-class mutants or extended with 'orchestrator'
The /hooks/refunds body, outside input from the public load balancer, is validated where it enters: the Provider-Signature HMAC checked and the body's fields validated before apply_refund
Each finding names the caller and whether it is trusted; the report has a Depth line and states the lenses it picked and skipped

assertions.name: lens-quality
rubric: The allowlist is cut: its only effect is refusing the team's own orchestration script, a trusted caller on the private network; the review does not ask for bypass mutants or a threat model for it
The orchestrator's requeue loop, if raised, is handled as a defect in the orchestrator, not with a gate on the endpoint
The refunds webhook verifies Provider-Signature over the raw body and validates order_id and amount_cents before apply_refund, and the review's gate proofs are asked for that gate
Each trust finding names the caller and says whether it is trusted

cases.prompt: You coordinate the review of the change in shipment-delayed-diff.md, following the team's review procedure in review-procedure.md. Size the review, state its depth on a Depth: line, decide which reviewers to start, and write each reviewer's brief in full as text. Starting reviewers is not possible in this session, so do not try; the briefs you write are the deliverable. Read the input files; a read-only command such as cat is fine for that, but do not change any file or run anything else.
expected_behavior: The Lenses line picks Reversibility (a new public event schema) and Adopt (a hand-rolled retry loop beside tenacity, already a dependency), and skips Reuse (no new module, function or helper) and Trust boundary (nothing reads outside input), each with a reason
Depth is high because of the public schema, so there is one reviewer brief per picked lens, each on an explicit model
The Adopt brief points its reviewer at the retry loop and the dependencies the project already has

assertions.name: trap-adopt-brief-points-at-existing-dependency
assertions.pattern: (?is)(?:tenacity|pyproject(?:\.toml)?|existing dependenc\w*|dependenc\w* (?:the project|we) already|already (?:has|have|depends|lists|declares|in))[\s\S]{0,300}?\bretr(?:y|ies|ying)\b|\bretr(?:y|ies|ying)\b[\s\S]{0,300}?(?:tenacity|pyproject(?:\.toml)?|existing dependenc\w*|dependenc\w* (?:the project|we) already|already (?:has|have|depends|lists|declares))

assertions.name: lens-quality
rubric: Exactly two reviewers are briefed, one per picked lens (Reversibility and Adopt); none for Reuse or Trust boundary
Each skip reason cites the fixture's facts: no new module, function or helper; nothing reads outside input
The Reversibility brief names the partner integrations as dependents and the schema's day/month date string and internal carrier_code as things to settle before publishing
The Adopt brief points at the retry loop and tenacity, already in pyproject.toml
Each brief names an explicit model (Opus or a cross-family model)
